implementation.name: original-v1-allocator-live-cached-blocks
implementation.scope: Original fixed virtual-address pool, expressed in the same twelve illustrative units. No growth, compaction, remapping, or pending device consumers. Snapshot (c) is split into two causal actions.
implementation.question: Why can six free units fail a six-unit request?

purpose: Why can six free units fail a six-unit request?

storyboard.label: All three tensors live
storyboard.description: A, B, and C each own one contiguous block. Every reserved unit is live.

storyboard.label: Release B
storyboard.description: B has no remaining consumers. Its four units become cached and reusable; reservation stays unchanged.

storyboard.label: Reuse two units for D
storyboard.description: D occupies the first half of B’s cached block. The unused remainder stays cached.

storyboard.label: Release A
storyboard.description: A’s final consumer finishes. Its block becomes reusable, but D separates it from the other free region.

storyboard.label: Request six contiguous units
storyboard.description: The allocator cannot combine separated free regions into one contiguous allocation under this fixed-pool policy.

guard: Reserved = live + reusable; request accepted only if largest contiguous free block fits.
